clue.text: Chief received energy charges

indicators.note: energy charges into the word, pushing its way inside

parts.note: if you had something you received it
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: The boss has been billed for power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges' looks like bills, but it means rushes in: E charges into HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Head and chief are synonyms for the leader, as in head of department.

clue.text: Conspicuous men — ten I suspect

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are not to be trusted in this order

explanation.surface: A detective picks out men who stand out, ten of them under suspicion.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent means prominent and noticeable, standing out above others.

clue.text: Remain at first diligent and agreeable

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of diligent is D
well can mean satisfactory or pleasing, as in 'all is well'

explanation.surface: Stay hard-working and pleasant to start with.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to stay or live in a place, an old-fashioned sense of remain.

clue.text: Men dance in uncle's premises

parts.note: chess pieces are called men, and pawns are the commonest
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Some men are dancing at their uncle's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker, so his premises are where goods are pledged for loans.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawnbroker was nicknamed uncle, so his shop is the uncle's place of business.

clue.text: Writer's verse abridged

indicators.note: an abridged text is shortened, here by its final letter

parts.note: a poem is a piece of verse

explanation.surface: An author's poem has been cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe was an American author of poems and tales.

clue.text: State is on top of those against cracking victory

indicators.note: the inner letters crack open the word for victory and sit inside

parts.note: a win is a victory

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece goes above the next

parts.note: taken as written
the cons are the arguments against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A state is atop its opponents, breaking through to win.
explanation.walkthrough: IS goes 'on top of' CONS in this down answer, and the result goes 'cracking' WIN, between W and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisconsin is one of the fifty United States, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Pupil finally performs choral works

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word

parts.note: the last letter of performs is S

indicators.note: works means the letters are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A schoolchild at last sings in choral pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' takes S from performs. 'Works' looks like a noun, compositions, but it rearranges CHORAL into CHOLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learner at school, in an older sense, as well as an academic.

clue.text: Flower shows using helpers, essentially around forty

indicators.note: around says these letters go round the number

parts.note: essentially means at heart: the middle letters of shows, using and helpers are O, I and P
XL is forty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A floral show relies on volunteers, roughly forty of them.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken 'essentially', the hearts of the three words give OIP, which goes 'around' XL.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxlip is a wild flowering plant of the primrose family, like the cowslip.

clue.text: Eternal smile set to change

indicators.note: set to change says the letters are ready to be put in a different order

explanation.surface: A permanent smile is about to alter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something timeless lasts for ever, unaffected by the passing of time.

clue.text: Reserved husband joins tea lady off and on

indicators.note: joins says the second piece is attached after the first
off and on means every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: the even letters of tea lady are E, L and D

explanation.surface: A man teams up with the woman who serves tea, now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Tea lady read 'off and on' gives ELD, which 'joins' H. A tea lady is the British office worker who brings round tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat that is held is kept back for someone, which is what reserved means.

clue.text: Male with case of laryngeal pain

indicators.note: with says the pieces go together

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: the case of a word is its first and last letters

parts.note: the outside letters of laryngeal are L and L

explanation.surface: A man with a sore throat is suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Hell is extreme suffering or torment, as in going through hell.

clue.text: Online pest pretty much exposed novelist

parts.note: a troll posts provocative messages on the internet

indicators.note: pretty much means almost all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: open means exposed, uncovered

explanation.surface: An internet pest has more or less unmasked a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope was a Victorian author of novels such as Barchester Towers.

clue.text: Tense philosopher's articles collected by bride

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
Jean-Jacques Rousseau was an 18th-century philosopher; the 's is read as 'has' joining the definition

explanation.surface: An anxious thinker owns things a bride has gathered.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the clothes and linen a bride gathers for her marriage.

clue.text: Trims back half of corn plaster

indicators.note: back means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: cuts are trims, as at the hairdresser

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is two of its letters, here the first two

explanation.surface: Someone cuts back half of a corn plaster on a foot.
explanation.walkthrough: CUTS read 'back' is STUC, and 'half of' corn is CO. 'Corn plaster' reads as a dressing for the foot, but 'plaster' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine plaster used for coating walls and decorative work.

clue.text: Cocaine from Chile distributed round centres in far north

indicators.note: round says the rearranged letters go round the others
letters distributed are spread around into a new order
the centres are the middle letters of each word

parts.note: the middle letter of far is A, and of north is R

explanation.surface: Cocaine from South America is handed out in the Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: CHILE 'distributed' gives CHLIE, which opens after CH to go 'round' AR, the 'centres in' far and north.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie is slang for cocaine, from the C of the NATO-style alphabet.

clue.text: Gutted Scrooge stifles copy writer

indicators.note: stifles means the outer letters smother the other word inside them
gutting a word removes its insides, leaving the first and last letters

parts.note: Scrooge gutted leaves S and E
to crib is to copy someone else's work

explanation.surface: A miser, devastated, suppresses a copywriter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' leaves SE from Scrooge, which 'stifles' CRIB. 'Copy writer' reads as one job, but copy gives CRIB and writer is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is a person who writes, especially one who copied manuscripts by hand.

clue.text: Lazy sort upset house, beginning to insult ballet company

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset means turned upside down, so read upwards

parts.note: a slob is a lazy, untidy person

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter

parts.note: the first letter of insult is I

explanation.surface: An idle person disturbs a house by starting to abuse the dancers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bolshoi is the famous Moscow theatre's ballet troupe.

clue.text: Murderer, fiend, regularly pursues two nincompoops

indicators.note: pursues means the following piece comes after the other

parts.note: an ass is a fool, and two of them give ASS twice

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter, here the second and fourth

parts.note: the even letters of fiend are I and N

explanation.surface: A devilish killer chases a pair of idiots at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a killer, especially of a prominent figure.

clue.text: Stigma of Communist leader abandoning Left

indicators.note: abandoning means the letter is dropped from the name

parts.note: Joseph Stalin led the Soviet Communist Party

explanation.surface: The disgrace of a Communist boss deserting the political left.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain on someone's character is a mark of disgrace, a stigma.

clue.text: Notify small group of intellectuals

indicators.note: a small group of the letters is taken from within the word

parts.note: the letters sit inside the word intellectuals, after its first three

explanation.surface: Inform a little circle of thinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell someone something is to inform them of it.

clue.text: Idiot suppresses second wind

indicators.note: suppresses means the word holds the other letter down inside it

parts.note: a twit is a foolish person

explanation.surface: A fool stifles a burp.
explanation.walkthrough: TWIT 'suppresses' S. 'Wind' suggests air or burping, but it is the verb rhyming with find: to coil or turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind a thread round something is to twist it, or a road can twist and wind.

clue.text: Incredible time, everything coming together

indicators.note: coming together says the pieces are joined

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: An amazing moment when it all falls into place.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is one that is hard to believe, so tall can mean unbelievable.

clue.text: View agreement rowing crew accepts

indicators.note: accepts means the crew takes the other word in

parts.note: an eight is a racing boat crew of eight rowers
yes expresses agreement

explanation.surface: A rowing team takes on board a look at a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of seeing, and view can mean sight or vision.

clue.text: Animal solvers caught

indicators.note: caught here means heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the clue addresses solvers as you

explanation.surface: Puzzle fans trapped a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' suggests capture, but it means caught by the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe is a female sheep, so an animal.

clue.text: Shaky cushy job having start delayed

indicators.note: having its start delayed means the opening letter is moved further back in the word

parts.note: a sinecure is a paid post with little work

explanation.surface: A wobbly easy job whose beginning is postponed.
explanation.walkthrough: SINECURE is 'having start delayed': its S moves back two places, so SIN becomes INS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insecure is not firmly fixed and could fall, which is to be unsteady.

clue.text: People in line humiliated, partly taken aback

indicators.note: taken aback means the letters are read backwards
partly means only part of the word is taken

parts.note: the letters sit inside humiliated, between HUMI and ED

explanation.surface: People in a queue are embarrassed and a bit startled.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail is a queue of people, or the end of a line of them.
